claims.claim: The Genesis genealogies (chapters 5 and 11) contain lifespan data that, when plotted against generation number, fit an exponential decay model with an asymptotic floor of approximately 93 years.
claims.plain_english: If you graph the ages at death from Adam to Joseph, the numbers drop in a specific pattern that math calls 'exponential decay,' and they stop dropping around 93 years.
claims.evidence_given: A table of lifespans from Genesis 5 and 11, a fitted exponential curve L(n) = L0 * e^{-n/τ} + L_floor, an R² of 0.888, and a chart showing data points and the fitted curve with L_floor ≈ 93.
claims.what_would_break_it: If the lifespan data were random, linear, or did not level off near 93; if a different curve fit gave a significantly different floor; or if the R² were much lower.

claims.claim: The exponential decay of lifespans is the signature of 'generational entropy' — a compounding degradation of informational fidelity (I_f) passed from parent to child, not a linear or random decline.
claims.plain_english: The reason lifespans drop faster at first and then slow down is that each generation inherits a little more 'wear and tear' from the previous one, like a photocopy of a photocopy getting worse each time.
claims.evidence_given: The shape of the curve (exponential vs. linear), the concept of informational fidelity (I_f) degrading at each generational remove, and the theological claim that the serpent's attack in Genesis 3 introduced noise into the channel between humans and God's original design.
claims.what_would_break_it: If the lifespan decline were linear or random; if a non-compounding mechanism could produce the same curve; if there were evidence that degradation does not accumulate across generations.

claims.claim: The asymptotic floor of ~93 years is not arbitrary but corresponds to a 'grace floor' — a minimum Logos-coupling (χ field ground state) that common grace maintains and that thermodynamics cannot breach.
claims.plain_english: The reason lifespans don't keep dropping to zero is that God's common grace sets a lower limit on how much 'disconnection' from the source of life a human body can have and still survive.
claims.evidence_given: The mathematical floor from the curve, the convergence with Psalm 90:10 (70-80 years) and modern life expectancy (~73 years), and the framework's concept of the χ field as a nonzero ground state analogous to the Higgs field's vacuum expectation value.
claims.what_would_break_it: If lifespans could decay below 70-80 years in any population; if the floor were shown to be an artifact of the data or fitting method; if a naturalistic mechanism (e.g., genetic bottleneck) fully explained the floor without needing a theological 'grace floor.'

claims.claim: Three independent sources — the exponential decay model (93 years), Psalm 90:10 (70-80 years), and modern global life expectancy (~73 years) — converge on the same lifespan floor, indicating they are measuring the same physical reality.
claims.plain_english: A math model, an ancient poem, and today's world health statistics all point to the same number range for how long humans can live, which means they're all detecting the same real limit.
claims.evidence_given: The model's floor of 93, the quote from Psalm 90:10 ('threescore years and ten... fourscore years'), and the modern average of ~73 years. The document presents these as three measurements converging on the same region of the number line.
claims.what_would_break_it: If the model's floor were significantly different from 70-93 (e.g., 50 or 120); if modern life expectancy were to rise well above 93 without a change in human biology; if Psalm 90 were shown to be about something other than a lifespan limit.

claims.claim: The Flood event reset some of the accumulated generational entropy, causing the exponential decay to restart from a lower baseline (Shem at 600) rather than continuing from the pre-Flood plateau (Noah at 950).
claims.plain_english: The big flood in Noah's time partially 'reset' the damage that had been building up, so lifespans after the flood started lower than before but then kept dropping again.
claims.evidence_given: The data table showing a sharp drop from Noah (950) to Shem (600), and the curve fit showing a restart of exponential decay after the flood marker. The document argues the reset is not complete because Shem still lives 600 years.
claims.what_would_break_it: If the post-flood data could be explained by a continuous curve without a reset; if there were no plausible mechanism for a reset; if the flood were not a real event or its timing were wrong.

claims.claim: Moses, writing Psalm 90 around 1400 BC, identified the lifespan floor (70-80 years) without any mathematical model, demonstrating an intuitive recognition of the asymptotic limit that modern curve-fitting confirms.
claims.plain_english: Moses figured out the same lifespan limit by just looking at people's ages, without using any fancy math — and he got it right, even closer than the computer model.
claims.evidence_given: The quote from Psalm 90:10, the model's floor of 93, and the claim that Moses 'was closer than the model' (70 vs. 93). The document asserts that Moses recognized the floor from observation of lifespans in his own time.
claims.what_would_break_it: If Psalm 90 were not written by Moses; if the verse were about something other than a lifespan limit (e.g., a metaphor for human frailty); if Moses had access to genealogical records that already contained the floor.

claims.claim: The Genesis lifespan data is not mythology or symbol but a 'measurement record' — the oldest biological dataset we have — that fits a specific mathematical model with high precision (R² = 0.888).
claims.plain_english: The ages in the Bible aren't just made-up numbers or symbols; they're real data that matches a scientific curve, making them the oldest recorded biological measurements.
claims.evidence_given: The R² value of 0.888 for the exponential fit, the data tables, and the argument that the pattern is 'not in dispute' because it's in the data. The document contrasts this with interpretations that treat the numbers as symbolic.
claims.what_would_break_it: If the fit were poor (R² < 0.7); if the data were shown to be symbolic (e.g., numbers based on numerology); if alternative interpretations (e.g., different chronologies or textual variants) produced different numbers that did not fit the curve.

claims.claim: The exponential decay of lifespans is a direct consequence of the Fall introducing thermodynamic time and the entropy arrow at Genesis 3, with the serpent's attack specifically degrading informational fidelity.
claims.plain_english: The reason lifespans got shorter over time is that when Adam and Eve disobeyed God, the world became subject to decay and 'running down,' and the serpent's lie messed up the way information about how to live properly was passed down.
claims.evidence_given: The exponential curve, the concept of informational fidelity (I_f), and the theological narrative of Genesis 3. The document links the serpent's question ('Did God really say?') to the introduction of noise in the information channel.
claims.what_would_break_it: If the Fall did not introduce thermodynamic time; if entropy accumulation were not heritable; if a naturalistic mechanism (e.g., genetic drift, mutation accumulation) could fully explain the curve without reference to a Fall.
